FINDING_ID: R5_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` can terminate the FSM before applying the adaptive fingerprint update for the just-completed round, because `update_fingerprints()` is guarded by `if not self.fsm.is_terminal`. This means the final observed evidence of the run is systematically excluded from the “live” capability state, even though the method documentation says fingerprints are updated “after each round” from actual output. The bug is cross-cutting: convergence/diminishing decisions are computed from the final round’s findings, but capability adaptation is not. Any caller that inspects post-run live fingerprints, exports them for future runs, or expects the terminal round to contribute to capability estimates gets stale state biased against later evidence.

FINDING_ID: R5_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` accepts `responses` and `findings` for any `round_idx` values but never enforces that they match `self.fsm.current_round`. `ModelResponse.round_idx` and `Finding.round_idx` are ignored during processing; all supplied records are attributed to `round_idx = self.fsm.current_round` when updating convergence, diminishing returns, failure history, and emitted events. A caller can therefore accidentally mix delayed or future responses into the wrong round, corrupting cumulative classes, novelty detection, underperformance persistence, and the event log without any error.

FINDING_ID: R5_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 2 (interface)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` does not enforce consistency between `responses` and `findings`: findings whose `model_id` is absent from `responses` are still incorporated into convergence and fingerprint updates, while responses from models with no associated findings are treated as normal. This creates an interface-contract hole across Areas 4, 5, and adaptive routing: a model can contribute findings without having produced a tracked response, or be penalized for no findings while another model’s orphan findings improve its live fingerprint. The artifact assumes findings are “extracted from responses,” but that invariant is never checked.

FINDING_ID: R5_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` can be called after the FSM has reached `TERMINAL`, because there is no terminal-state guard. The manager will continue returning new allocations from active models even though `process_round()` would subsequently raise on `fsm.transition(...)` if called again. This leaves the orchestrator with an incoherent contract: the system can still plan work after declaring itself stopped. The flaw spans orchestration and FSM lifecycle management.

FINDING_ID: R5_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` treats timeout detection and underperformance detection as orthogonal mechanisms, but only transport/protocol failures emit manager events; UNDERPERFORM returns `FailureType.UNDERPERFORM` silently. As a result, `DynamicManager.process_round()` may downgrade roles or log persistent underperformance without the real-time monitoring interface ever surfacing the triggering event, despite `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` existing explicitly. This is not just a missing event cosmetic issue: it breaks the advertised PM monitoring contract by making one failure class invisible in the streaming interface.

FINDING_ID: R5_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` can return `RecoveryAction.DOWNGRADE_ROLE` for underperformance, but neither `FailureHandler` nor `DynamicManager.process_round()` implements any semantics for that action. The only post-round role change is unconditional `role_assignment.reassign(...)`, which ignores the selected recovery action entirely. Thus the recovery policy table claims a differentiated control path that never exists operationally. This is a cross-area gap between failure policy and role assignment, deeper than merely noting that some events are missing.

FINDING_ID: R5_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` records success/failure history only for model IDs present in `responses`. Any active model omitted from `responses` for a round is absent from `failures`, does not get `record_failure(..., False)`, does not get failure detection, and does not contribute to underperformance persistence. Missing responses are therefore silently interpreted as “not observed” rather than as an operational anomaly, which biases both role reassignment penalties and failure escalation. This edge case is distinct from prior findings about arbitrary IDs: even valid active models can disappear from accounting with no signal.

FINDING_ID: R5_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `ManagerEventStream.emit()` buffers the event before invoking the external callback. If the callback raises, the event remains recorded in `_buffer` and `_all_events` even though the higher-level operation that emitted it may abort mid-flight. This yields non-atomic event semantics: consumers inspecting the stream later can observe events for actions that failed to complete because the callback exception propagated. Since `DynamicManager` and `FailureHandler` do not catch callback exceptions, external observer failures can partially commit internal observability state and interrupt business logic.

FINDING_ID: R5_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.get_cumulative_classes(round_idx)` and related methods implicitly treat all missing intermediate rounds as empty by iterating `for r in range(round_idx + 1)` and defaulting to `[]` when a round was never registered. This permits non-contiguous round insertion without any validation, so adding data for rounds 0 and 3 silently fabricates rounds 1 and 2 as empty in cumulative metrics. The result is understated novelty/rate behavior and distorted gamma estimation under sparse or retried orchestration histories.

FINDING_ID: R5_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 2 (interface)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
DESCRIPTION: The public `RoundResult.failures` contract is internally inconsistent with the rest of the manager API because it only contains entries for `responses.keys()`, not for all active or allocated models. A caller cannot distinguish “no failure,” “no response,” and “not scheduled” from the result structure alone. Since `RoundResult` is supposed to capture “all outputs needed for cross-area communication,” this omission makes the result insufficient as a standalone round ledger.
